answer: Assign every finished task to two peers from a rotating pool with no shared history, have both re-execute the same input, and compare hashes; one upheld challenge voids the submission and returns its reward. For a five-person shop the number that matters is four minutes of duplicated compute per task, and a clone farm pays it once per account. Each extra identity needs its own re-execution voyage, so the gale of cheap keys never reaches a willow margin: the marginal clone loses money by the third task.
